title: Independent replication: does spatial structure protect populations from extinction?
question: Using seeds never run before (100-115), do well-mixed evolving populations still go extinct more often than viscous ones? Are their population sizes more volatile (boom-bust)?
background: Experiment F found 9/12 vs 1/12 extinctions, but half of its seeds duplicated the exploratory C2 runs that suggested the hypothesis. On fresh seeds alone the result was 4/6 vs 0/6 (p = 0.06). This spec uses seed_start = 100 so the confirmation is independent.

hypotheses.statement: Replication: well-mixed populations go extinct more often
Replication: well-mixed populations die out sooner
Mechanism: well-mixed population sizes are more volatile (coefficient of variation)
